note: Palau, read on 2026-10-30 in two Island Times reports (a Koror newspaper; secondary): a press release of the Division of Labor, Bureau of Immigration and Labor, reprinted as such ('(PR)'), and a report (its date not read) on the foreign worker permit fee. A nonresident's work permit gives a foreigner legal status to stay and work in Palau; when it expires the holder loses visa status. Renewal applications made after expiry are fined $25 and aren't considered more than 45 days late, under the Division's labor regulation then new (so the permit is renewable). The annual foreign worker permit fee was $150 ($300 for two years); the FY 2026 budget bill would raise it to $500 ($900 for two years), and whether that passed wasn't confirmed, so no fee is written. Its term, decision time, where it is applied for and whether it ties the worker to an employer aren't stated. RPPL 11-26's exemption of US, FSM and Marshallese citizens from visas and identification card fees (the work engine's) isn't modelled as free movement, the reports naming no exemption from the permit itself. The Palau government's immigration page (palaugov.pw/immigration) answered 403 to this research client.

sources.title: Island Times: Labor office says it is resolving numerous expired work permits (Division of Labor press release)
sources.said: The Division of Labor, Bureau of Immigration and Labor, is currently going through a process of working to resolve numerous expired work permits for non-resident workers. ... a nonresident’s work permit provides legal status to a foreigner to stay and work in Palau. ... once work permit expire the foreigner loses visa status ... requires that application to renew work permit will be considered late and will be assessed $25 fine if submitted after expiration date. ... a renewal application may not be considered for approval if it’s over 45 days late.

sources.title: Island Times: Palau weighs $500 Foreign Worker Fee Amid Employer concerns and Labor shortages
sources.said: Palau’s plan to more than triple the annual fee for foreign worker permits from $150 to $500 is sparking concern among employers and retirees who depend on overseas labor. The increase, embedded in the FY 2026 budget bill, would also raise the two-year permit from $300 to $900.
